findings.criterion: `gh repo view navapbc/rebar --json description` returns the approved description exactly.
findings.detail: This criterion requires a live GitHub API readback confirming the exact description text. The ticket has a comment from RebarBotNava stating 'Exact readback matches the approved 236-character description,' but this is a non-codebase criterion (GitHub repository metadata) that requires a concrete attestation with a verifiable specific (e.g., the exact description text returned, a timestamp, or a command output). The comment does not quote the exact returned description string, nor does it provide a command output transcript or timestamp. The criterion is tagged as codebase-verifiable (no [non-codebase] tag), but the evidence lives entirely outside the repository. The ticket's `file_impact` is empty and `no_file_impact_reason` confirms 'GitHub repository metadata only. No repository file changes.' There is no repository file to verify this against. The comment is an assertion of completion without the specific verifiable output required.
findings.remediation: Record a ticket comment that includes the exact output of `gh repo view navapbc/rebar --json description --jq .description` (the full description string), the timestamp of the readback, and the actor who ran it, so the attestation contains a verifiable specific matching the approved text.
findings.title: No verifiable readback of exact GitHub description

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
